KOPERASI DESA MERAH PUTIH is the institutional analogue of China's revived supply-and-marketing cooperative network: ~83,000 units legally established by July 2026, ~35,000 targeted operational by August 2026 (15,845 physically complete, 19,539 under construction), each designed as a modern retail outlet plus pharmacy, village clinic, logistics warehouse, office and micro-finance unit, with ~1.6 million administrator roles projected. It is the most ambitious state village-commerce programme in Indonesian history and its execution will largely determine whether Indonesia gets the Chinese outcome or the KUD outcome.

MBG (MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS) is the fiscal analogue of China's rural demand-stimulus instruments: IDR 335 trillion budgeted for 2026 (up ~96% from IDR 171 trillion in 2025), IDR 101.1 trillion absorbed in H1 2026 across 63.13 million recipients, with ~70% spent on locally sourced inputs from farmers, fishers, MSMEs and BUMDes.

THE WARUNG-TECH WAVE (Mitra Bukalapak, Mitra Tokopedia, GudangAda, Ula, BukuWarung, AwanTunai, Modalku, SRC) is Indonesia's attempt at the Chinese B2B distribution digitisation layer — combined funding of ~USD 180 million for Ula/BukuWarung/GudangAda alone, and B2B BNPL GMV projected to ~USD 5.89 billion by 2030 — though Bukalapak's 2025 exit from physical-goods marketplace shows the first-generation model did not work as designed.

E-COMMERCE GEOGRAPHY: tier-2/3 locations rising from ~40% of Indonesian e-commerce in 2021 to ~50% by 2025, in a market moving from ~USD 90.35 billion (2025) to ~USD 104.21 billion (2026), with TikTok Shop specifically activating second- and third-tier consumers who were previously inactive online.

confidence_level: Tinggi (High) for the core factual base — Chinese official statistics (NBS, MOFCOM policy documents), Mixue's audited disclosures, Indonesian BPS macro data, and company store counts are all well-sourced and mutually consistent. Sedang (Medium) for the Indonesian sinking-market-specific figures, because Indonesia has no official tier-2/tier-3 classification and no equivalent of China's county retail statistics — 'tier-2/3 contributes ~50% of e-commerce' comes from commercial research firms, not statistical agencies, and the warung count is an association estimate rather than a census. catatan_kontradiksi_data:
(1) KOPDES TARGET DATES CONFLICT ACROSS SOURCES. Official statements variously placed completion at March 2026, April 2026, August 2026 for ~35,000 operational units, and end-2026 for all 80,000 — with ~83,000 legally established but only 15,845 physically complete as of mid-2026. Legal establishment, physical construction and actual operation are being reported interchangeably by different ministries, which materially inflates apparent progress. Treat only the 'operational and transacting' number as real.
(2) WARUNG COUNT INCONSISTENCY. Figures of 3.5 million, 3.9 million and '2.2 million closed since 2007 from 6.1 million' circulate together; these are APKLI association estimates, not a statistical census, and the Ministry of Trade has publicly disputed the causal attribution to modern retail. The direction is well established; the magnitude is not.
(3) MIXUE INDONESIA STORE COUNT VS CLOSURES. Reports simultaneously describe Indonesian outlets approaching 2,600 and growing, and 428 overseas store closures in 2025 with Indonesia among the most affected — the company did not disclose the Indonesian closure count, so net versus gross expansion in Indonesia cannot be reconciled from public data.
(4) MIXUE GLOBAL FIGURES SPAN DIFFERENT PERIODS. 46,000 / 53,000 / 59,823 store figures appear across sources referring to different reporting dates (2024 IPO prospectus, H1 2026 interim, FY 2026); they are not contradictory but are frequently quoted without period labels.
(5) ALFAMART/INDOMARET STORE COUNTS. Q3-2025 company figures (20,925 and 23,441) versus the 'combined 44,366' cited in February 2026 imply almost no net growth over the interim, which is inconsistent with stated opening plans — likely a difference between Indonesia-only and including overseas/other formats.
(6) CHINA RURAL RETAIL GROWTH READ-ACROSS. Rural retail growth (4.1%) exceeding urban (3.6%) in 2025 is genuine but modest — some commentary overstates it as a boom when it is better described as relative resilience within a soft national market. Similarly, '80% of FMCG growth from tier-3 and below' is a commercial research figure whose base and methodology are not public.
(7) INDONESIAN 'TIER' DEFINITIONS ARE NOT STANDARDISED. Different research houses classify Indonesian cities differently, so the ~50% tier-2/3 e-commerce share is not directly comparable to Chinese tier definitions.
(8) MBG ECONOMIC IMPACT ESTIMATES VARY WIDELY, from BRIN's IDR 14.5-26 trillion GDP contribution to far larger political claims; the offsetting cost of Dana Desa reallocation is rarely netted out in the same analysis.
